nbzinbPate

nbzinbPate fits

  • negative binomial (NB2) regression with nbreg(), comparable to MASS::glm.nb(), and
  • zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression with zinbreg(), comparable to pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin"),

with all of the estimation implemented from scratch. No general-purpose optimizer (optim(), nlm(), …) and no GLM fitter (glm(), lm(), …) is used:

  • NB: iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for the coefficients with θ\theta fixed, alternated with Newton-Raphson for log⁡θ\log\theta with the coefficients fixed.
  • ZINB: an EM algorithm. The E-step computes the posterior probability that each zero is a structural zero. The M-step fits a fractional-response logistic regression for the zero model and a weighted NB regression for the count model, both by IRLS.
  • Standard errors: (X⊤ŴX)−1(X^\top \hat W X)^{-1} and {−H(θ̂)}−1/2\{-H(\hat\theta)\}^{-1/2} for NB. For ZINB, the inverse observed information, computed from an analytic Hessian of the observed-data log-likelihood with respect to (β,γ,log⁡θ)(\beta, \gamma, \log\theta).

This package was written for the STA 651 Module 2 final project (Fall 2026).

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("brandonp8/nbzinbPate")

The package only depends on base R (stats). The reference packages MASS, pscl, AER and numDeriv are needed only to run the tests.

Example

The bioChemists data (from pscl) record the number of articles published by 915 biochemistry PhD students.

library(nbzinbPate)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
m_nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(m_nb)
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
#> 
#> Pearson residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -1.2677 -0.8754 -0.2613  0.4983  6.6573 
#> 
#> Coefficients (NB2 with log link):
#>              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  0.256144   0.137348   1.865 0.062191 .  
#> femWomen    -0.216418   0.072636  -2.979 0.002887 ** 
#> marMarried   0.150489   0.082097   1.833 0.066791 .  
#> kid5        -0.176415   0.052813  -3.340 0.000837 ***
#> phd          0.015271   0.035873   0.426 0.670326    
#> ment         0.029082   0.003214   9.048  < 2e-16 ***

#> Number of observations: 915   Outer iterations (IRLS + Newton): 5
# Zero-inflated NB: count model before "|", zero-inflation model after it
m_zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | kid5 + ment,
                  data = bioChemists)
summary(m_zinb)

The usual methods work: coef(), vcov(), logLik(), AIC(), BIC(), fitted(), residuals(), nobs(), and predict(), including predict(m_zinb, newdata, type = "response" / "count" / "zero").

AIC(m_nb, m_zinb)
#>        df      AIC
#> m_nb    7 3135.917
#> m_zinb 10 3126.387
predict(m_zinb, newdata = data.frame(fem = "Women", mar = "Married",
                                     kid5 = 0, phd = 3, ment = c(0, 10, 40)),
        type = "zero")
#>            1            2            3 
#> 2.940806e-01 9.440864e-04 1.102945e-11

Agreement with the reference implementations

On bioChemists and AER::NMES1988, the estimates match MASS::glm.nb() and pscl::zeroinfl() far more closely than the project tolerances require.

  • NB vs glm.nb(): the coefficients, their standard errors, θ\theta and the log-likelihood agree to about 1e-10. SE(θ\theta) agrees to about 1e-6, because glm.nb() evaluates it at the second-to-last Newton step for θ\theta.
  • ZINB vs zeroinfl(): the coefficients, standard errors and log⁡θ\log\theta agree to about 1e-5 or better, and the log-likelihood to about 1e-9.

The package tests (tests/testthat/) check this agreement automatically.
